crops.name: Winter wheat
crops.overview: The highest-yielding Irish cereal, used for feed and milling.
crops.ireland: Ireland has some of the highest wheat yields in the world; best on deep, well-drained medium/heavy soils in the south and east.

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

conventional.N: 170–230 kg N/ha total (Teagasc, by soil N index and yield potential), split Feb–May
conventional.S: Sulphur 15–25 kg/ha on light soils/high-yield crops
conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: N from clover/grass ley or legume preceding crop, cattle FYM or composted manure (≤170 kg organic N/ha/yr whole farm), slurry in spring. P/K from manures; permitted rock phosphate and permitted potassium sulphate (natural origin) if soil test low. Lime to pH 6.5.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Irish rainfall (750–1,200 mm) normally meets needs; irrigation not used. Avoid waterlogging over winter.
water.critical: Stem extension to grain fill (May–July) is when drought hurts yield, mainly on light soils.

harvest.storage: Dry to 14–15% moisture (malting 12–13%), cool and aerate; check for insects.

conventional.pests: Aphids/BYDV (autumn insecticide or BYDV-tolerant variety), slugs after OSR/grass, Septoria, rusts, mildew, Ramularia/net blotch (barley), take-all in second cereals. Use a T0–T3 fungicide plan based on variety ratings and Teagasc/DAFM advice.
conventional.weeds: Pre-/early post-emergence herbicide in autumn, follow-up in spring for cleavers, wild oats, brome, blackgrass where present.

organic.pests: Choose varieties with high disease ratings (DAFM Recommended List); later sowing to cut BYDV risk; wider rotations (no second cereal) against take-all; variety mixtures; undersown clover. No synthetic fungicides or insecticides.
organic.weeds: Stale seedbed, delayed sowing, higher seed rate, comb-harrowing/tine weeding at 3–5 leaves, competitive tall varieties.

crops.rotation: Avoid second and third cereals (take-all, grass weeds). Good after grass, beans, OSR or potatoes.

organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Irish rainfall (750–1,200 mm) normally meets needs; irrigation not used. Avoid waterlogging over winter.
water.critical: Stem extension to grain fill (May–July) is when drought hurts yield, mainly on light soils.

harvest.storage: Dry to 14–15% moisture (malting 12–13%), cool and aerate; check for insects.

conventional.pests: Aphids/BYDV (autumn insecticide or BYDV-tolerant variety), slugs after OSR/grass, Septoria, rusts, mildew, Ramularia/net blotch (barley), take-all in second cereals. Use a T0–T3 fungicide plan based on variety ratings and Teagasc/DAFM advice.
conventional.weeds: Pre-/early post-emergence herbicide in autumn, follow-up in spring for cleavers, wild oats, brome, blackgrass where present.

organic.pests: Choose varieties with high disease ratings (DAFM Recommended List); later sowing to cut BYDV risk; wider rotations (no second cereal) against take-all; variety mixtures; undersown clover. No synthetic fungicides or insecticides.
organic.weeds: Stale seedbed, delayed sowing, higher seed rate, comb-harrowing/tine weeding at 3–5 leaves, competitive tall varieties.

crops.rotation: Avoid second and third cereals (take-all, grass weeds). Good after grass, beans, OSR or potatoes.

crops.name: Maize (forage/silage)
crops.overview: High-energy silage for dairy and beef; needs warm, sheltered southern/eastern sites.
crops.ireland: Marginal in the north-west; plastic mulch extends the range.

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

planting.window: Late April–mid May (under film in most of Ireland)

conventional.N: 70–140 kg N/ha after slurry (Teagasc maize guide)
conventional.S: Sulphur 15–25 kg/ha on light soils/high-yield crops
conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 5.8–7.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: Responds well to slurry and FYM incorporated before sowing; legume or ley before. Avoid plastic if certification rules restrict it — check with your body.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 5.8–7.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Needs ~350–450 mm in season; dry, warm summers favour it. No irrigation in Ireland normally.

harvest.signs: Grain at "half milk-line", whole crop 30–35% DM
harvest.storage: Clamp at 30–35% DM, roll well and seal.

conventional.pests: Frit fly, slugs, birds at establishment; eyespot and fusarium. Plastic mulch (degradable film) is widely used in Ireland to gain heat units.
conventional.weeds: Pre-emergence herbicide, often applied under film.

organic.pests: Sow into warm soil, bird scaring, robust seed rate, rotation. Organic growers avoid treated seed.
organic.weeds: Inter-row hoeing and finger weeding; stale seedbed; under-sown grass after canopy closure.

crops.rotation: Can follow itself a few years but soil structure suffers; good after grass.

crops.name: Buckwheat
crops.overview: Pseudo-cereal; fast smother crop and loved by bees.
crops.ireland: Frost-sensitive; seed crop is risky in Ireland.

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

conventional.S: Sulphur 15–25 kg/ha on light soils/high-yield crops
conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 5.0–7.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: Usually no fertiliser. Legume covers fix N for the next crop.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 5.0–7.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

conventional.pests: Few; avoid brassica covers before brassica crops (clubroot). Destroy chemically or mechanically before the next crop as allowed under the Nitrates rules.
conventional.weeds: Glyphosate is commonly used to destroy covers — not permitted in organic.

organic.pests: Choose species to break pest cycles; mix species.
organic.weeds: Destroy by rolling/crimping, grazing, mowing and shallow incorporation.

crops.rotation: Fits between crops; Nitrates Regulations require green cover on tillage ground after harvest in many cases.
